Haiku 5.5 bills a prompt past 100k tokens at five times its base rates,
and Copilot passes the same list price through.

Long-context models accept 1M tokens natively, with no beta header. This is
the working window we run them at, capped well below that ceiling to bound
cost and latency, and aligned with `WIDE_PLAN_CONTEXT_WINDOW`. Unlike the
200k entries, it is an *input* budget: `max_output_tokens` is granted on top
of it rather than carved out of it.

A request whose prompt runs past this many tokens bills in full at twice
the input and cache rates and one and a half times the output rate. The
wide window sits above it, so the last stretch before compaction always
pays the long rate.

Working window for the long-context OpenAI models, gpt-5.6 and gpt-6.
Deliberately below what the API accepts — gpt-6 advertises 1,050,000 —
because the window is what caudra fills before compacting, and cost and
latency scale with it.

The output limit of every Gemini model in the table. On Gemini 4 it is the
most one streaming request returns. Asking for more starts long decode,
which stops with `CONTINUATION` and expects the client to resume.

Gemini 4 and 3 take a `thinkingLevel` and cannot turn thinking off, so
`off` runs at the lowest level. Argon and 3.8 Flash reject `minimal`.

for offline runs). The API wins via discovered metadata; these mirror

alone, so the tier comes from here even once discovery has landed.
